newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka extends amnesty for surrender of guns.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka extends amnesty for surrender of guns.

text.p: Sri Lanka has extended an amnesty for the surrender of illegal weapons until March 15, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.
The amnesty, originally scheduled to lapse on Tuesday, was extended at the request of political leaders, a ministry statement said.
It said more than 750 unlicensed firearms had been handed over to the police since the amnesty, primarily aimed at politicians and their supporters, was announced late last month.
About 170 firearms have been seized since police launched a nationwide crackdown to curb political violence ahead of March 21 local government elections, it added.
The Indian Ocean island's gun culture became a key public issue after a young ruling People's Alliance coalition legislator was gunned down last month.

A member of parliament of the main opposition United National Party (UNP) and a former UNP mayor are among the suspects detained over the killing during a roadside quarrel between alliance and UNP supporters.

Politicians and political activists in Sri Lanka own guns, many of them unlicensed, to guard themselves against possible attack by Tamil rebels who are fighting a separatist war in the island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year.

A former Tamil rebel leader on Wednesday said he plans to appeal the government crackdown on unlicensed firearms, arguing that he was specially susceptible to attacks by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Douglas Devananda, member of parliament and leader of the Eelam People's Democratic Party (EPDP), told Reuters the firepower he had was insufficient to protect himself from the LTTE.
"My problems are different from other politician's. The arms I have are not sufficient for my security," Devananda said.
Devananda's fortress-like home in suburban Colombo was attacked by suspected LTTE guerrillas in October 1995.
Devananda, who wears two pistols concealed beneath his shirt, escaped, but four bodygyards were killed in the attack.
